elements.element: Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel.

elements.element: The Services performance warranty remains effective for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 imposes the Services warranty without a time limit, and Section 19.2's 90-day cutoff is expressly limited to the relevant Deliverable. Section 19.4 provides remedies for breach of Section 19.1.

elements.element: Deliverables and software materially conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 warrants that Services, which include hosted software under Section 1.7, and Deliverables materially conform to documentation and agreed specifications; Section 19.2 repeats the Deliverable warranty.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty remains effective for at least 12 months.
elements.evidence: No provision states a 12-month software warranty. Hosted software receives an untimed Services warranty under Sections 1.7 and 19.1, but Section 19.2 expressly limits each Deliverable, potentially including a software Deliverable, to 90 days and bars correction or refund afterward. The required 12-month coverage is therefore not established for all software.

elements.element: Repair is available as a remedy for breach of warranty.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor promptly to repair a nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: Replacement is available as a remedy for breach of warranty.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor promptly to replace a nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: A refund is available as a remedy for breach of warranty.
elements.evidence: If Vendor cannot re-perform, repair, or replace within a reasonable period, Section 19.4 permits Customer to terminate the affected item and receive a refund of the Fees paid for it.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 refers to industry standards, the Agreement, and Order Forms, but contains no operative warranty of compliance with applicable laws.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services, software, and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no malicious-code warranty or equivalent prohibition.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by extending the Deliverable period from 15 to 90 days and limiting the cutoff to the affected Deliverable, leaving the untimed Services and hosted-software warranty in Section 19.1 operative. It does not reach the preferred position because it lacks an unambiguous 12-month warranty for all software, a legal-compliance warranty, and a malicious-code warranty. The changes are targeted and preserve the existing remedy structure, although the overlap between the untimed Section 19.1 warranty and the time-limited Section 19.2 warranty creates some classification ambiguity for software Deliverables.
